core_obligations: Set up the boundary maps (proof lines 4752-4755): put N_n = H^{p+1}(C, I^n F_{n+1}) and let delta_n : M_n -> N_n be the boundary map of the short exact sequence 0 -> I^n F_{n+1} -> F_{n+1} -> F_n -> 0.

Show the images form a graded submodule (proof lines 4756-4773): for s in M_n and f in I^m, the displayed commutative diagram of short exact sequences gives delta_{n+m}(fs) = f delta_n(s), so the direct sum of the Im(delta_n) is a graded submodule of the direct sum of the N_n.
Use the ascending chain condition to choose finitely many generators s_j at levels n_j and let c be their maximum (proof lines 4774-4776).

Conclude the stable image (proof lines 4776-4784): for n > c and s in M_n, write delta_n(s) = sum f_j delta_{n_j}(s_j) with f_j in I^{n-n_j}; then s - sum f_j s_j dies under delta, so it lifts to M_{n+1}, and since the f_j s_j map to zero in M_{n-c} the images of M_{n+1} and M_n in M_{n-c} agree, which is Mittag-Leffler in the stable form.
proof_roadmap: Introduce the boundary maps delta_n from the short exact sequences cutting out F_n.
Verify the graded compatibility delta_{n+m}(fs) = f delta_n(s) via the commutative diagram.
Apply the ascending chain condition to get finitely many generators of the graded module of the images.
For n beyond the largest generating level, express delta_n(s) using those generators and lift the corrected element to the next level.
Read off the equality of images in M_{n-c}, which is the Mittag-Leffler condition.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a Mittag-Leffler criterion: an ascending chain condition on the graded piece formed by the H^{p+1}(C, I^n F_{n+1}) forces the inverse system M_n = H^p(C, F_n) to satisfy Mittag-Leffler (statement lines 4730-4749). The substantive step is to make the direct sum of the images of the boundary maps into a graded module: one has to write the commutative diagram of short exact sequences induced by multiplication by an element f of I^m and read off delta_{n+m}(fs) = f delta_n(s) (proof lines 4756-4773). The chain condition then produces finitely many generators at levels n_j, and for n beyond their maximum an arbitrary element is corrected by a combination of the generators so that it lifts to M_{n+1}, which yields the stable-image statement (proof lines 4774-4784). The claim is H2: one graded-module bookkeeping argument, with the diagram as its non-formal input.
